BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City DILG NO 30 HON. JULIUS D. GLORIA Sangguniang Bayan Member San Ricardo, Southern Leyte Dear Hon. Gloria: This pertains to your earlier letter requesting for this department's opinion on the alleged persistence of the Local Chief Executive of San Ricardo, Southern Leyte, to collect toll fees in a private seaport. The relevant facts and issues submitted were quoted in toto as follows. I. "On 14 June 2023, the Sangguniang Bayan had unanimously approved the enactment of "An Ordinance Levying a Transport System Fee on all Motor Vehicles Entering the Municipal Road Leading to Any Seaport in the Municipality of San Ricardo, Province of Southern Leyte" (Please see Annex "B"). Unfortunately, however, our Local Chief Executive vetoed said ORDINANCE (A COPY OF THE VETO LETTER IS ALSO ATTACHED HERE AS Annex "C". Is the veto of the LCE valid? What makes the ordinance inconsistent to Section 133 of the Code when it does not impose pass through fees upon goods or merchandise? What happens to the vetoed enacted ordinance if the sanggunian fails to override the same?" 2. "The LCE and most of the members of the sanggunian strongly believe that by virtue of that Contract of Lease, the LGU can now collect toll fees. Another ordinance entitled "An Ordinance Authorizing to Lease of Private Property to be used as an access way to Temporary Seaport of San Ricardo" (please see Annex "D") was recently introduced in lieu of the enacted ordinance and this has been approved on the first reading last 26 June 2023. Granting that all the pre-requisites in the enactment of an ordinance are complied with and with the approval of the LCE, can the LGU then legally collect toll fees in that private port?" 3. "As the Contract of Lease stipulates a retroactive effect, is it valid? Aren't the terms and conditions disadvantageous on the part of the LGU?" 4. "Should the Contract of Lease found to be invalid, how does it affect to the ordinance and in its implementation since it is heavily referenced in its making? What are the possible implications if they insist to implement the ordinance despite the advice of its legality?" A thorough evaluation of the facts and issues submitted prompts us to address the propriety of the subject matter instead, which renders answering the specific questions futile. "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

We discuss succinctly. The LGU's act of levying a "Transport System Fee" on all motor vehicles that enters its territorial jurisdiction and heading towards any seaport within said LGU is previously governed by DILG-ARTA-DOF JMC No. 2021-01, OMNIBUS GUIDELINES ON THE SUSPENSION OF LGU IMPOSITION AND COLLECTION OF ILLEGAL FEES AND TAXES RELATIVE TO THE TRANSPORT OF GOODS AND PRODUCTS; and now, by the recently issued Executive Order No. 41 s. 2023, PROHIBITING THE COLLECTION OF PASS-THROUGH FEES ON NATIONAL ROADS AND URGING LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO SUSPEND THE COLLECTION OF ANY FORM OF FEES UPON ALL TYPES OF VEHICLES TRANSPORTING GOODS UNDER SECTION 153 OR 155 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160 OR THE "LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991". Please be advised that pursuant to Section 1 of E.O. No. 41 s. 2023, the imposition and collection of toll fees and charges upon all motor vehicles transporting goods or merchandise, while passing through any national road and such other roads not constructed and funded by LGUs are prohibited pursuant to Section 133 (e) of R.A. 7160. While for those imposed upon all motor vehicles transporting goods and merchandise through any local public roads constructed and funded by LGUs pursuant to Section 155 of R.A. No. 7160, the suspension or discontinuance of collection is likewise strongly urged or encouraged. In the herein case, there is an argument that by virtue of the contract of lease entered into between the LGU and a private individual for the privately-owned land which is considered as an access way to Temporary Seaport of San Ricardo, Southern Leyte, the LGU can now collect toll fees. Considering that access way is privately owned, it is neither a national road nor a local road constructed and funded by said LGU. Hence, our evaluation on this peculiar case is subjective and dependent on the following circumstances: 1 2. If there are other publicly-owned access ways to the seaport but are not made available obviously for the purpose of imposing the toll fees, then, the contract of lease on the "privately-owned land turned into access way" and the imposition of Transport System Fee or Toll Fee were made to circumvent the government's implementation of DILG-ARTA-DOF JMC No. 2021-01 , the policy that suspends the imposition of pass-through fees enforced during the time the lease was executed. It is likewise a violation of Section 133 (e) of R.A. No. 7160 as the same is in the guise of "Transport System Fee or Toll Fee" If there are no roads or other publicly-owned access ways to the seaport, and the "privately-owned land turned into access way" is the only possible access to the private seaport, then the LGU's act of leasing the privately-owned land is deemed as the LGU's resolution to provide and facilitate the flow of goods and merchandise to and from its territorial jurisdiction as well as the nearby LGUs. In this case, the imposition of "Transport System Fee" is a legitimate imposition strictly in the nature of "Toll Fee" under Section 155 of the Local Government Code. Section 15 applies only to facilities funded by the LGU but that fact that the LGU leases the privately-owned land to turn it into an access way, the same falls within the context "facilities funded by the LGU." The imposition on the basis of Section 155 of the Local Government Code, in this case, will not be deemed as "pass-through fees" imposed in the guise of toll fees" prohibited by Section 133 (e) of the LGC. In that case, however, the Page 2 of 3

amount of said toll fee to be charged shall only cover the use of the access-way (which constitute the payment for the lease of the private land) and that reasonable amount that will help recoup the costs of road construction or access way maintenance. Regardless, however, we emphasize that E.O. No. 41 is still in effect and as such LGUs are encouraged to suspend imposition. The rationale behind the same is to avoid additional cost to the price of basic goods and merchandise that may be shifted to consumers at the hype of the present inflation. Now, as to matters concerning the validity of the contract of lease entered into on the subject access-way, the answer varies depending on the attendance and/or applicability of the two different circumstances mentioned above. Relative to this, it is prudent to remind that any contract entered into in violation of, or contrary to, a law or a public policy, is void ab initio. This opinion is being issued without prejudice to contrary opinion of competent authorities/agencies or any judgement that may be rendered by the proper court on the matter. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, ORITY OF THE SECRETARY. ATTY.
